newsitem.title: USA: GM TO STREAMLINE CORPORATE SUPPORT FUNCTIONS.
newsitem.headline: GM TO STREAMLINE CORPORATE SUPPORT FUNCTIONS.

text.p: General Motors Corp said Wednesday it formed a new unit to consolidate and streamline corporate support functions.

The new unit, called the Enterprise Activities Group, will be headed by Matthew Cullen, GM's director of worldwide real estate. Cullen engineered the automaker's $75 million purchase of Detroit's Renaissance Center for use as its new global headquarters.
GM said Cullen's group will take a fresh look at GM support operations and gather as many units as logically fit together under one organizational structure.

"In a company the size of General Motors, many of our support functions do enough business with internal GM units to rank them among the largest players in their industry," said GM Vice Chairman Harry Pearce said in a statement.

"Matt's entrepreneurial success in reengineering our real estate operation to ensure a strategic focus and benchmark quality makes him an ideal candidate to look for similar opportunities to increase competitiveness and quality among other service areas of the enterprise," Pearce said.

Cullen's first assignment will be to identify those General Motors business units that will make up the Enterprise Activities Group. GM said a significant percentage of its corporate support funtions will be handled by the new organization, including the Worldwide Real Estate group.
Cullen, 41, will continue to manage the transition of the Renaissance Center into GM's global headquarters, the automaker said.
